scientific_name: Chrysanthemum x morifolium 'Mammoth Dark Bronze Daisy'

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in early spring so roots establish well before winter; part of the University of Minnesota's Mammoth series bred for reliable perennial survival without winter mulch as far north as zone 3.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, moderately fertile soil; Mammoth Dark Bronze Daisy builds a dense, naturally rounded mound and needs no pinching to stay full and compact. Coppery bronze single daisy flowers with sunny yellow centers cover the plant in a heavy flush from early into late fall, giving one of the warmest, most autumnal color tones in the Mammoth series. Bred at the University of Minnesota specifically for cold hardiness, it overwinters unprotected in the open garden where typical florist-type pot mums are killed outright. Divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring to maintain vigor.

scientific_name: Chrysanthemum x morifolium 'Mammoth Dark Pink Daisy'

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in early spring so roots establish well before winter; released in 2006 as part of the University of Minnesota's Mammoth series bred for perennial survival without winter mulch as far north as zone 3.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, moderately fertile soil; Mammoth Dark Pink Daisy forms a tidy, self-branching mound without pinching. Deep, saturated pink single daisy flowers with gold centers open in a dense late-summer to early-fall flush, a richer and darker pink than the softer tones of other pink-flowered garden mums. Its University of Minnesota parentage gives the roots exceptional cold tolerance, allowing the plant to overwinter unprotected well north of where typical greenhouse-grown pot mums survive. Divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring to renew vigor.

scientific_name: Chrysanthemum x morifolium 'Mammoth Twilight Pink Daisy'

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in early spring so roots establish well before winter; an early release in the University of Minnesota's Mammoth series bred for perennial survival without winter mulch as far north as zone 3.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, moderately fertile soil; Mammoth Twilight Pink Daisy grows into a dense, rounded mound without any pinching required. Its single daisy flowers open pink with a distinctive darker purple-toned eye at the center, a two-tone effect that sets it apart from the plainer gold-centered pinks elsewhere in the Mammoth series, blooming heavily from late summer into fall. As part of the University of Minnesota's cold-hardy breeding program it returns reliably year after year without winter protection where many pot mums die out. Divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring.

common_name: Icicle Igloo Chrysanthemum (Hardy White Cushion Mum)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in early spring or fall; Icicle Igloo is part of the patented Igloo series of dwarf, naturally mounding garden mums bred for uniform habit and garden hardiness.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, moderately fertile soil; Icicle Igloo grows into a dense, low, uniformly rounded cushion without pinching, staying noticeably shorter and tighter than typical border mums. Crisp white double flowers cover the mound in a heavy late-summer into fall display, the clean white contrasting well against the dark green foliage. As part of the Igloo series bred for dependable garden performance, it holds its compact mounded shape through the season and is well suited to the front of the border or mixed containers. Divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring to maintain vigor.

common_name: Sizzling Igloo Chrysanthemum (Hardy Yellow Cushion Mum)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in early spring or fall; Sizzling Igloo is part of the patented Igloo series of dwarf, naturally mounding garden mums bred for uniform habit and garden hardiness.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, moderately fertile soil; Sizzling Igloo forms a dense, low, naturally mounded cushion without pinching. Bright golden-yellow double flowers smother the plant in a heavy late-summer into fall flush, giving a hot, saturated color that lives up to the cultivar's name. Like the rest of the Igloo series it keeps a tight, uniform, rounded habit through the season rather than sprawling, making it useful for edging, mass planting, or fall container combinations. Divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring to keep the planting vigorous.

common_name: Pumpkin Igloo Chrysanthemum (Hardy Orange Cushion Mum)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in early spring or fall; Pumpkin Igloo is part of the patented Igloo series of dwarf, naturally mounding garden mums bred for uniform habit and garden hardiness.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, moderately fertile soil; Pumpkin Igloo grows into a dense, low, uniformly rounded cushion without pinching. Flowers open a warm red hue and mature to a glowing pumpkin-orange with a bright yellow button eye, so a single plant carries a subtle blend of red and orange tones as older and newer blooms open together through the late-summer into fall display. As part of the Igloo series it holds its tight, compact mounded shape through the season, making it a strong match for the deep oranges and golds of the fall landscape. Divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring to maintain vigor.

common_name: Ice Pink Igloo Chrysanthemum (Hardy Pink Cushion Mum)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in early spring or fall; Ice Pink Igloo is a later patented addition to the Igloo series of dwarf, naturally mounding garden mums bred for uniform habit and garden hardiness.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, moderately fertile soil; Ice Pink Igloo forms a dense, low, freely branching cushion without pinching, keeping an upright, uniformly mounded outline through the season. Decorative-type flowers open a bright, cool-toned reddish pink and cover the plant heavily from late summer into fall. As with the rest of the Igloo series, its compact, self-supporting habit and good winter hardiness make it well suited to the front of the border, edging, or fall container plantings rather than the taller, floppier mums that need staking. Divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring to keep plants vigorous.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in early spring or fall; Stadium Queen is a football (exhibition-type) mum bred for enormous individual blooms rather than dense garden coverage.

directions: Plant in full sun in rich, well-drained soil; disbud side buds and stake tall stems, since Stadium Queen is a football-type mum grown for spectacular single blooms rather than a mounded floral display. Each incurved flower opens 6 to 7 inches across in a bronzed red-orange that reveals a bright yellow button center as the petals unfurl, the classic homecoming-corsage color of traditional football mums. It flowers in mid to late fall on sturdy upright stems that carry the oversized blooms well above the foliage. Divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring and feed regularly through summer to support the large flower size.
